hook: An old fishing harbour full of nautical gear: find each thing on the quay or the water, then give it its article.
intro: A picture hunt instead of a deck: one old fishing harbour with 32 things to find on the water and on the quay, every one a precise word from the sea and the docks — der Poller, die Seilwinde, der Duckdalben, das Steuerhaus, der Hummerkorb. The prompt asks Wo ist der Fender? The prompt asks for one object, and you tap it in the picture. Each find shows its label, coloured by its gender, then leaves a small tick in that colour, so you can see what you have already found. A tap on the wrong object tells you what you hit and you keep looking; after three misses the right one is shown. Once you have passed a run, the hunt turns harder: the prompt hides the article (Wo ist ___ Fender?), and after the find you choose der, die or das yourself. No object is asked twice in the same run.
tips[0].title: Compounds in the harbour: the last part decides
tips[0].text: Harbour words are almost all compounds. Schiff + Glocke: die Glocke, so die Schiffsglocke. Steuer + Haus: das Haus, so das Steuerhaus. Hummer + Korb: der Korb, so der Hummerkorb. Find the last word and you have the article.
tips[0].check.why: The last part is der Ring, so the whole word is der Rettungsring.
tips[1].title: Same first part, different article
tips[1].text: Steuer- makes no promise about gender: das Steuerrad (das Rad) and das Steuerhaus (das Haus) are neuter, but on land die Steuer is a tax. Likewise Fisch- gives die Fischkiste but das Fischernetz. Only the last part counts.
tips[1].check.why: The last part is das Netz, so it is das Fischernetz.
tips[2].title: Many -er things on the quay are der
tips[2].text: Things in -er that work or hold something tend to be masculine here: der Poller, der Fender, der Anker, der Kutter, der Eimer, der Kanister. Read each label aloud with its article — the blue ticks pile up along the quay edge.
tips[2].check.why: Anker is masculine; the plural is the same: die Anker.
remember[0]: The last part of a compound sets the article: der Turm → der Leuchtturm, die Glocke → die Schiffsglocke.
remember[1]: Many -er things on the quay are der: der Poller, der Fender, der Anker, der Kutter.
remember[2]: Some plurals change the vowel: das Floß → die Flöße, der Seesack → die Seesäcke.
